Service:  Trauma Surgery

CHIEF COMPLAINT:  Status post fall with abdominal trauma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:  Patient is an 85-year-old female
with history of hypertension, who fell on to a chair after
tripping on a rug at home.  The patient hit her left upper
abdomen on a chair during the fall.  On arrival in the ED,
the patient was evaluated by a CAT scan of the abdomen which
revealed a grade 3 splenic laceration with a large amount of
blood in the abdomen.  The patient was orthostatic in the
Emergency Department.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
1. Hypertension.
2. Lymphoma status post chemotherapy (five years ago).
3. Depression.
4. Right femoral neck fracture.
5. Recent upper respiratory infection treated with Z-Pak.

fixation for femoral neck fracture in [**2110**].

MEDICATIONS:
1. Aspirin.
2. Calcium.
3. Sertraline.
4. Recent Zestril.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:  Patient's vital signs on presentation
were 37.1, 103, 156/71, 22, and 97% on room air.  The patient
was in no apparent distress.  Heart rate was regular.  Lungs
were clear.  Abdomen was soft, slightly distended, nontender
with no guarding, rebound, or peritoneal signs.  Rectal
examination was guaiac negative, and the pelvis was stable.
Neurologic examination was within normal limits.

LABORATORIES:  White count was 17.2, hematocrit 32.3 down to
29.5, platelets were 278.  Chemistries were normal.
Coagulation revealed an INR of 1.1, PT of 13, and a PTT of
21.3.  Liver function tests were within normal limits.

IMAGING:  Chest x-ray revealed no pneumothorax and no
fractures.

CAT scan of the abdomen revealed a splenic laceration, grade
3 with hemoperitoneum.

HOSPITAL COURSE:  Following evaluation in the ED, the patient
was admitted to the ICU for continued monitoring.  Serial
hematocrits were drawn which were ultimately essentially
stable.  The patient received a unit of blood on hospital day
#2 in an attempt to improve her overall hematocrit.  Her
hematocrit remained essentially stable.  Serial hematocrits
continued to be drawn and on hospital day #3, the patient
received 2 units of blood with an appropriate increase in her
hematocrit from 31-32 range to about 36.

Patient was transferred to the regular floor on hospital day
#3.  Serial hematocrits continued to be drawn and remained
stable.  Patient remained on bed rest.  Urine cultures drawn
in the Emergency Department revealed the patient had a
urinary tract infection and she was started on a course of
ciprofloxacin.

By hospital day #6, the patient had been advanced to a
regular diet and her activity level had been increased with
the patient being allowed out of bed.

On hospital day #7, patient was ambulating freely on the
floor.  She was started on a miconazole vaginal suppository
for suspected yeast infection for complaints of vaginal
discharge.

On hospital day #8, the patient was deemed stable and ready
for discharge.  The patient was started on an empiric course
of Flagyl for a possible Clostridium difficile infection
following complaint of increased stool output.  The patient
was afebrile with stable vital signs on discharge.

DISCHARGE CONDITION:  Stable.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
1. Miconazole combopack x2 more days.
2. Sertraline 50 mg half tablet once a day.
3. Timolol eyedrops.
4. Metoprolol 50 mg to take a quarter tablet twice a day.
5. Flagyl 500 mg p.o. t.i.d. x7 days.

FOLLOWUP:  Patient was to followup in the Trauma Clinic one
week following discharge.

MISCELLANEOUS:  The patient was to receive a visit from a
nurse for home safety evaluation following discharge.  The
patient was also given a script for a bedside commode to be
used at home.  The patient was instructed not to drive for
two weeks and to remain at home for a week following
discharge.

cells, 4 units of fresh frozen plasma and 2 bags of
platelets.

Postoperatively, the patient was transferred to the Intensive
Care Unit and required full ventilatory support on the
ventilator.  Due to his large transfusion, the patient was
suffering from coagulopathy.  Also, intraoperatively, due to
the graft placement, a T-tube was placed at the bile duct and
served as a drainage conduit.  A pigtail catheter was placed
outside the bile duct to drain out any biloma that was
accumulating in the abdomen.  A nasogastric tube was placed.

ventilator, he underwent a tracheostomy in the Intensive Care

graft infection.

boost his nutritional status.  A central line was placed.

day number nine.  On postoperative day number ten, the
patient was started on tube feeds, initially at 10 cc/hour
which the patient tolerated well.  Tube feeds were continued
and increased up to goal.

and the patient was placed on a standing dose of Haldol to
control his agitation.  While in the Intensive Care Unit, we
essentially administered supportive care.

noted to be steadily improving and he was stable enough to be
transferred on a regular floor.  Prior to transfer, the
patient had an echocardiogram which showed 4+ regurgitation.
Cardiology was consulted prior to the Intensive Care Unit
transfer and recommended cardiac medication for the
congestive heart failure while in the Intensive Care Unit.

The patient was transferred to the regular floor on [**2172-12-11**].  While on the floor, the patient was afebrile with
stable vital signs.  We obtained a swallow study on the
patient and it appeared that the patient had begun to
tolerate regular oral intake and the swallow study team had
recommended to start the patient on a soft liquid diet.  It
was recommended that patient start on soft solids and regular
liquids for a diet as tolerated.  Meanwhile, we would
continue the tube feeds.

The patient's tracheostomy was decannulated on [**2172-12-14**] and the patient tolerated the decannulation well.  Prior
to discharge, he was breathing without the tracheostomy,
saturating at 97% without any difficulties.

Cardiology had scheduled the patient for an magnetic
resonance angiogram to look at his coronary arteries.
However, due to the patient's large body habitus and
claustrophobia, the study could not be done.  Cardiology
recommended medication for the patient's 4+ regurgitation
found on the echocardiogram.
